gaps.sentence: After introducing herself, she went on ___ the main findings.
gaps.hint: move on to a new activity
gaps.explanation: go on + to-infinitive = do something after finishing something else.

gaps.sentence: I tried ___ the shelf up, but it was too heavy.
gaps.explanation: try + to-infinitive = attempt, make an effort.

gaps.sentence: I'm learning ___ the guitar at the moment.
gaps.explanation: learn takes the to-infinitive (learn how to play).

gaps.sentence: My boss won't ___ me take Friday off.
gaps.explanation: let + object + bare infinitive: won't let me take. (allow/permit take to: allow me to take.)

gaps.sentence: It took me ages ___ used to the new keyboard.
gaps.explanation: it takes time + to-infinitive: took me ages to get used to the keyboard.

gaps.sentence: The scheme aims ___ younger visitors to the museum.
gaps.explanation: aim + to-infinitive: aims to attract (aim at + -ing is also possible in BrE).

gaps.sentence: They agreed ___ the fence between the two gardens.
gaps.explanation: agree takes the to-infinitive: agreed to mend.

gaps.sentence: This new timetable will mean ___ earlier trains.
